paper.title: Adaptive Incentive Design in Dynamic Principal-Agent Problem via Kernelized Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Dynamic principal-agent contract design with stochastic agent utility (kernelized bandit with heteroscedastic noise)
unmapped: Contract space X=[0,1]^m; reward is principal's utility (v-x)_i with outcome i drawn from production function under the agent's hidden stochastic best response
Each round the chosen contract is sampled ell>1 times to estimate the mean and the heteroscedastic variance
Noise variance function lies in an RKHS of a kernel kappa^v with norm bounded by B_v (known); variance-estimate noise is sub-Gaussian with known proxy
settings.definition_quote: Formally, in each round $t$, the principal posts a contract $x_t \in \mathcal{X}:= [0,1]^m$ ... $\tilde{y}_t= \tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}(x_t) + \tilde{\varepsilon}(x_t)$, where $\tilde{\varepsilon}(x_t)$ is assumed to be a zero-mean \textit{heteroscedastic} noise ... $\Tilde{R}_T= T\Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{P}*} - \sum_{t=1}^T \Tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}(x_t)$

algorithms.name: Heteroscedastic GP-UCB (with Neural Network / Arcsin kernel)

conditions: tilde U^PA in RKHS H_k of the arcsin kernel with norm <= B (S)
noise variance in RKHS of kappa^v with norm <= B_v (Assumption 4.2)
variance-estimate noise eta(x_t) is rho_eta(x_t)-sub-Gaussian with known proxy, independent in time (Assumption 4.3)
contract space [0,1]^d (paper's m is the dimension)
tuning: beta_t as in eq. (beta_t) with confidence delta

source.label: main_theorem
source.quote: Consider $\tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}} \in \mathcal{H}_k$ with bounded RKHS-norm (i.e., $\|\tilde{U}^{\mathrm{PA}}\|_{\mathcal{H}_k} \le B$) and sampling model in \eqref{feedback_eq} with unknown variance ... satisfies Assumptions~\ref{var_proxy_assumption} and~\ref{noise_assumption}. ... Setting $\lambda=1$ in \eqref{beta_t}, the cumulative regret $\Tilde{R}_T$ ... is bounded as $\mathbb{P}\left[\Tilde{R}_T \leq \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{T}(\log T)^{m+1}\right)\right] \geq 1 - \delta$

results.notes: Paper's m (contract dimension) mapped to canonical d. Constants (log(1/delta), B, ell, chi_u) hidden in O. Proof derives gamma_T = O((log T)^{m+1}) via Proposition 4.4 eigenvalue tail bound and plugs into Makarova et al. Theorem 1. Regret counts per-round utility although ell samples are drawn per round.
